changelog: The proof-of-origin token now survives a restart, and a cached answer no longer outlives it. The token the television mints is what lifts YouTube's sixty-second wall on trailer streams; it was held only in memory, so every Jellyfin restart threw it away - and a restart happens on every plugin install, which meant trailers fell back to 360p until somebody next opened the app on a television. It is written to configuration now, masked on the page, and read back at start-up. Separately, a resolution cached before a token arrived is no longer served after one does: a token does not merely make the next resolution better, it makes the last one wrong, so the held token carries a generation and a cached answer from an older one is ignored.
description: Lightweight virtual TV channels: deterministic schedules over your own library, tuned in via normal direct playback at the live position. No transcoding, no tuner emulation.
name: LiteTV Channels
